bibliographic.title: Critical dialogical accountability: From accounting-based accountability to accountability-based accounting
bibliographic.citation_apa: Dillard, J., & Vinnari, E. (2019). Critical dialogical accountability: From accounting-based accountability to accountability-based accounting. Critical Perspectives on Accounting, 62, 16-38. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cpa.2018.10.003

methodology.method_family: critical theoretical framework development in social and environmental accounting (SEA)
methodology.study_design: conceptual-theoretical article proposing a normative and descriptive accountability framework
methodology.sector: social and environmental accounting; public and private sector institutions
methodology.technology_context: accounting and disclosure systems; mentions Enterprise Resource Planning software platforms; no LLM, generative AI, or conversational AI systems

eligibility.exclusion_reason: The article is a theoretical accounting paper on institutional accountability. It does not address LLMs, generative AI, chatbots, agents, RAG, or technical conversational systems; uses dialogue/conversation only in institutional accountability discourse.
eligibility.decision_rationale: Strong conceptual contribution on accountability, governance, dialogue, contestation, and pluralism in institutional settings, but zero evidence in the provided text of LLM-based or conversational AI systems in regulated environments. Relevant only as foundational contextual theory for accountability constructs, not as central or supporting evidence for the review scope.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Python triage marked central_candidate due to governance and dialogue keyword matches, but LLM dimension scored 0/3; manual adjudication needed to confirm whether foundational accountability theory should be retained in the corpus.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal reflects quality as a conceptual SEA article based on provided excerpts. Transferability to LLM conversational governance in regulated settings is very low because the technology context is accounting systems, not AI.

cerqual.explanation: Internally coherent and adequately developed for accounting accountability theory, but methodological and substantive relevance to LLM conversational governance is very limited in the supplied text.

coding.theme: Critical dialogical accountability in pluralistic institutions

synthesis.main_claim: Institutional accountability should be reconceptualized through critical dialogical accountability, designing accounting systems around accountability requirements of diverse constituencies rather than extending traditional financial accounting disclosure.
synthesis.contribution: Offers a descriptive and normative definition of accountability recognizing power, pluralism, and dialogue, and proposes accountability-based accounting as an alternative to accounting-based accountability.
synthesis.limitations: Provided text does not empirically evaluate implementations, does not address AI or conversational technologies, and applicability to LLM governance remains indirect and unclear.
synthesis.use_in_review: Retain only as foundational contextual theory for accountability, dialogue, contestation, and governance constructs; exclude from central or supporting evidence on LLM conversational governance.
